title: What Jesus Did After Rising — Acts 1:3
paragraphs: What Jesus Did After Rising — Acts 1:3

He didn’t rise just to prove a point.
He stayed… to prepare a people.

Forty days.
That’s what Acts of the Apostles 1:3 tells us.

Forty days of a resurrected Jesus walking, teaching, revealing—
not to crowds chasing miracles,
but to disciples still wrestling with doubt.
He could have ascended that same morning.
But He didn’t.
Why?

Because resurrection wasn’t the finish line.
It was the beginning of a mission.

He showed them His scars.
Not hidden. Not erased.
Glorified wounds—proof that pain redeemed becomes power released.

He spoke about the Kingdom of God.
Not politics. Not revenge. Not overthrow.
Kingdom.
But here’s what we miss…
They still didn’t get it.

They asked, “Lord, will You restore the kingdom to Israel now?” (Acts 1:6)
They wanted crowns.
Jesus offered calling.
They expected takeover.
Jesus promised power—but not the kind they imagined.
“Wait,” He said.

Wait for the Spirit.
Wait for heaven’s fire.
Wait until weak men become witnesses.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because even after the resurrection—
they were still confused, still flawed, still slow.
And Jesus stayed anyway.

He didn’t cancel them.
He completed them.

He doesn’t rush broken people into purpose.
He walks with them until truth burns clear.
That same Jesus is still patient with you.

Still revealing.
Still restoring.
Still calling.

Your confusion doesn’t disqualify you.
Your delay doesn’t disinterest Him.
If you’re still here—He’s still working.

Forty days of proof.
A lifetime of purpose.

And then He ascended…
not to abandon—
but to send.
Because the story was never about staying with Him physically.

It was about Him living in us—through the Spirit—
turning ordinary people into living evidence of resurrection power.
So don’t rush your process.

Let Him teach you.
Let Him show you His scars.
Let Him reframe your expectations.

And when the Spirit comes—
you won’t just believe.
You’ll burn.

From confusion to commission—
because Jesus doesn’t just rise…
He raises people with Him.
